co_old_mill_area.blurb: Old Mill is a group of cliffs in Staunton State Park in Colorado, divided into Roughneck Wall, Black Creek Wall and the north and south faces of Sawmill Crag. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, with a solid trad minority and hardly any bouldering. Grades centre on 5.10 and 5.11, with a smaller handful of easier lines from 5.7 to 5.9 and a few at 5.12 and 5.13. Roughneck sits high above the others near an old sawmill site and mixes trad and sport lines. Across the park, the cliffs are described as featured rock with incipient cracks, so protection can be sparse and the climbing rewards careful route reading.

ma_milford_bouldering.blurb: Milford Bouldering is a woodland bouldering area in eastern Massachusetts, near Milford and Hopkinton. The boulders are scattered through the trees in separate clusters, so expect some walking between them. Quarry Land, Power Line Boulders, Milford North and Hillside are the main groups, with smaller ones such as Atomic Boulder and Vietnam. Almost all of it is bouldering, with a very even spread of difficulty: most problems fall between V0 and V4, and there is a solid layer of harder ones into the upper grades up to V8.

nj_mt_tammany.blurb: Mt. Tammany is the main climbing section of Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, on the New Jersey side at the southern end of the park beside the Delaware River and Interstate 80. The rock is quartzite, and the climbing is overwhelmingly traditional, mostly one or two pitches, with a few boulder problems, some top-rope lines and winter ice. Grades run from 5.3 up into the 5.12 range, with the bulk of routes between 5.7 and 5.10. There are more than twenty separate cliffs and walls, including Triumverate Wall, The Great Arch and Eldorado Wall. The Delaware Water Gap is described as one of the oldest climbing areas in the country.

ut_hellgate_cliffs.blurb: Hellgate Cliffs is a set of steep white limestone towers on the north side of Little Cottonwood Canyon, in the Central Wasatch near Snowbird, at roughly 8,800 feet. Climbing is mostly bolted sport, with some routes that want a small rack and a few trad, aid and ice lines at Main Hellgate. Most routes are 5.9 or harder, centred on 5.10 and 5.11, with a few easier ones. Tower One is mostly sport and Tower Two mixes trad and sport. East Hellgate is mostly sport on pockets and edges, with a blend of powerful moves and finesse. Loose rock is a known issue, especially in early to mid summer, so wear a helmet.

vt_shipyard.blurb: Shipyard is a bouldering area in Bromley Forest in southern Vermont, with a cluster of boulders sitting on and beside a powerline. Bromley Forest's rock is gneiss, and its pages say it holds some of the best problems in southern Vermont. Everything here is bouldering, with a broad spread from V0 into double digits; most problems fall between V0 and V6, with a steady supply of harder ones above. Breadloaf, The Monolith, United States of Banana and Tomahawk are among its larger groupings, and there are more than twenty named sub-areas in all. The problems are described as fun and varied in difficulty.

va_forest_the.blurb: The Forest is a bouldering area along the Blue Ridge Parkway in central Virginia, near Charlottesville, at about 2,700 feet. It is described as the largest concentration of greenstone boulders on the parkway. The boulders fall into two sections: a Main Area with Big Boy, Crossroads and Gumby, and a Ridgeline with Greenstonia, the Mushroom Area and Aqua Boulder. Greenstone along the parkway ranges from soft and fragile to very solid, with sharp edges and flakes. All of the climbing here is bouldering, from V0 to double digits, with most problems between V1 and V6 and a good number of harder ones.
